title: A Vision-Based Measurement Perspective on Vision–Language Models for Drone Presence: Mis-Calibrated, Not Blind_supp1-3754169.pdf
authors: Young Jae Kim
abstract: We treat a vision–language model (VLM) as a vision-based measurement (VBM) instrument whose measurand is drone presence in externally cued electro-optical/infrared (EO/IR) crops from the Anti-UAV-RGBT corpus, and report its trueness, precision, and uncertainty under one fixed prompt and explicitly stated negative-sampling protocols. Zero-shot, a Qwen2.5-VL-3B instrument records recall 0.007 at a false-positive rate (FPR) of 0.000—apparently blind—yet under the same prompt its latent yes/no decision margin attains an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.704, rising to 0.907 at the 7B scale: the presence signal survives while the reported decision collapses. We formalize this as mis-calibration and recover the instrument in three stages: (i) the zero-shot reading is prompt-dominated and near-useless; (ii) a single margin threshold learned only on adjustment recordings and frozen lifts 7B recall to 0.560 at a realized 4.8% FPR without fine-tuning; (iii) low-rank adaptation (LoRA) restores the decision. A negative-control battery then bounds the first adapted instrument: its specificity keys to crop geometry, not drones (FPR 0.954 on size-matched negatives and 0.959 on in-domain thermal confusers, against 0.000 on its own fixed-geometry protocol)—false-alarm behavior is a joint property of the instrument and the negative-sampling procedure. Re-adjusting with geometry-matched negatives, mined confusers, and all six EO classes yields the final instrument: recall 0.897 (recording-cluster interval 0.810 to 0.981) with FPR 0.005/0.037 under the matched protocols, margin AUC at least 0.97 on all three, and recall 0.943 at a realized 6.4% FPR under the frozen adjustment threshold, pooled over the three declared negative protocols. The audit-hardened operating point re-exposes the dominant uncertainty: its between-recording recall SD is 0.13, so the between-condition term governs even the final instrument. Confidence calibration is a verified procedure: Platt scaling learned on adjustment data reduces the zero-shot held-out expected calibration error from 0.385 to 0.150, and after adaptation the raw readout is already near-calibrated (pooled 0.033; per-protocol up to 0.097). All headline intervals are cluster-robust over the ten independent test recordings; frame-level intervals understate the zero-shot 7B uncertainty 7.1-fold.
